Roofing in Bedford, Texas

Bedford treats roof work seriously: a permit for repairs and replacements alike, and a city inspector at the end. A free phone line, answered day and night, puts you through to an independent roofer working in Bedford.

Call (469) 649-7066 Bedford's permit steps
  1. Home
  2. Service Areas
  3. Bedford

How a Bedford roof job moves through City Hall

Roofing in Bedford, TX comes with more city oversight than in some neighboring towns. The City of Bedford requires a permit for all roofing replacement or repairs, not just full tear-offs, and it sends an inspector out when the job is done.

  1. The roofer registers. Contractors register with the city through its online permit portal, and the registration is renewed each year. A homeowner working on their own homestead is the one exemption.
  2. The permit is issued first. The city says the permit must be issued before work starts. A remodel permit is added if the framing or roof pitch changes.
  3. The permit stays on site. It is kept at the job until the final inspection, so you should be able to see it.
  4. The city inspects the finished roof. Bedford performs a final roof inspection. Ask the roofer to tell you the result, and keep a copy for your records and any future sale.

Building Permits and Inspections is at 1805 L. Don Dodson Drive, Building C, and answers at 817-952-2140. The city's roofing page also mentions state licensing, yet no such state license for roofers exists in Texas, so ask the office what it actually checks when a roofer registers.

From a ranch town of 475 to a busy Mid-Cities suburb

The city's own budget history says settlers reached the Bedford area around 1860, the Bedford Boys Ranch opened after World War II, and the town incorporated on January 22, 1953, with about 475 people on roughly two square miles.

Then it filled in. By 1970 Bedford had passed 10,000 residents, and the decade that followed brought an industrial park, shopping centers and the opening of DFW Airport next door. The population reached about 20,800 by 1980 and about 44,000 by 1990. The old Boys Ranch land, meanwhile, became a city park.

A look back by the Bedford Citizen notes that ranch and Cape styles were the favorites in the 1950s. Much of the town's housing followed in the 1970s and 1980s, so many Bedford roofs have been replaced at least once, and a roofer should be ready to talk about layers, decking and attic airflow on an older house.

Hail reports logged in and near Bedford

The Storm Prediction Center keeps a daily log of spotter and public reports. These are preliminary, but they show what Bedford roofs have taken.

August 1, 2021

Golf-ball hail reported near Forest Ridge Drive and Highway 183 on the southwest side of Bedford, with quarter-size hail near Bedford Road and Highway 121.

May 27, 2024

That evening, baseball-size hail was reported a mile north of Bedford and hen-egg hail, two inches across, a mile southwest, along with golf-ball reports in town.

After a storm like either one, walk the yard rather than the roof. Note dents on gutters, vents and the air conditioning unit, look for shingle bits on the lawn, and photograph everything with the date before you call your insurer.

Roof work Bedford homeowners most often need

On a town of 1950s through 1980s houses, the calls tend to be repairs on aging roofs, full replacements once a roof wears out, and storm damage after a spring squall line.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Six things to ask a roofer about a Bedford job

  • Is your City of Bedford registration current for this year?
  • Will you pull the permit before tear-off and leave the card on site?
  • Who meets the city inspector for the final, and will I get the result?
  • Counting the old layers, how many are up there, and what does a replaced sheet of decking add to the bill?
  • Will your insurance agent send me your liability certificate directly?
  • If this is a claim, where is the Texas deductible notice in the contract?

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Bedford roofing questions

Does Bedford TX require a permit for a roof repair, or only a new roof?

Both. The City of Bedford says a permit is required for all roofing replacement or repairs, issued before work begins and kept at the job until the final inspection. If the framing or the roof pitch changes, a remodel permit is needed as well. Ask your roofer to show you the permit card before the first shingle comes off.

How can I tell if a roofer is registered in Bedford?

Call Building Permits and Inspections at 817-952-2140 and ask. Contractors register through the city's online permit portal, the registration renews each year, and the city has published lists of registered general contractors. A roofer that is not registered cannot pull the permit your job needs. See also the guide to checking a Texas roofer.

Does hail hit Bedford often?

Often enough to watch for. Storm Prediction Center logs show golf-ball hail near Forest Ridge Drive and Highway 183 on August 1, 2021, and on May 27, 2024, a baseball-size report a mile north of Bedford with hen-egg hail a mile southwest. Those are preliminary spotter reports, but stones that size can bruise and crack shingles. Signs you can spot without a ladder are on the hail damage page.

Can I re-roof my own Bedford house without a contractor?

The city exempts a homeowner working on their own homestead from contractor registration, but the permit and inspection still apply, and roof work is dangerous. Climbing, tearing off and nailing on a steep roof in Texas heat is a job for a roofing crew with fall protection. Let the roofer you hire pull the permit in its own name.
